observations.body: Jesus drives sellers and animals from the temple, rejects making his Father’s house a market, and answers with a saying about destroying and raising the temple of his body.
observations.label: Jesus disrupts the temple market and names his body

observations.body: The passage presents Passover, animals, money, zeal, sign demand, destroyed temple, body, and resurrection memory as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: Passover, animals, money, zeal, sign demand, destroyed temple, body, and resurrection memory

observations.body: The passage places temple and body beside Passover, animals, money, zeal, sign demand, destroyed temple, body, and resurrection memory.
observations.label: temple and body

payload.posture: Read John 2:13–22 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the action challenges the market setting while the narrator separately explains the body saying
payload.title: Jesus disrupts the temple market and names his body
